text:
Maria T.: quick async standup — API edge / routing / auth / rate limits

Maria T.: yesterday: finished the route rewrite PR for the customer-proxy. deployed to staging and smoke-tested 30m. saw a small increase in 429s on one service (svc-b).
Maria T.: blockers: need an opinion on whether to tighten the burst window (current: 2s) or raise per-route tokens for svc-b. also need a quick CR review on the rewrite (PR #438).
Maria T.: today: will run a short canary with token-bucket adjustments + push CR fixes.

Alex R.: looking now at PR #438, will leave inline comments by EOD. saw the 429s in the staging logs too — looks like a short-lived token exhaustion from the mobile clients.
Alex R.: suggestion: soften the burst to 3s and increase per-route refill to 10 req/s for svc-b, then monitor for 30m.

Chris P.: fyi I rotated the auth-jwks yesterday morning (rotation id: r-2026-03-15). No failures reported in prod auth logs, but double-check your canary uses the new keyset.
Chris P.: if you want a quick test token: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST" https://auth.internal/validate`

Samir K.: pushed a small fix to the rewrite to preserve X-Forwarded-Host header (was dropping it in some proxy hops). that should help the svc-b routing match and avoid fallback routes that hit stricter limits.
Samir K.: also added a short-lived metric `edge.route.match.miss` — watch for spikes during the canary.

Maria T.: @Alex R. thanks — can you post the exact command you used to generate the staging load? want to replicate locally.
Alex R.: sure — `wrk -t4 -c200 -d60s --script=mobile.lua https://staging-edge.example.internal/svc-b/` (mobile.lua simulates warm burst behaviour).

Leo H.: quick question — is it safe to change the per-route quota without touching the global tenant bucket? we had incidents where tenant-level buckets masked per-route increases.
Maria T.: good call — for the canary I'll only change the route-level bucket (no tenant-level changes). if we need higher steady throughput we'll coordinate a tenant bump during off-peak.

Chris P.: ping @Maria T. if you want me to temporarily whitelist the canary traffic in the auth proxy (so tokens bypass rate enforcement) — I can toggle a flag for a 1-hour window. only do this if the 429s are noise and not real client overload.
Maria T.: hold on that for now — we want to surface real behavior. I'll request whitelist only if the route tweak doesn't reduce 429s.

DeployBot: deployment started by Maria T. · staging · edge-rewrite-pr-438 · 1765440300
DeployBot: smoke tests: PASS · 1765440350

Maria T.: canary started at 1765440400 — adjusting burst to 3s and refill to 10 req/s for svc-b. watching metrics: edge.route.match.miss=0, auth.429s=downsampled. will report back in ~20m. :eyes:

Alex R.: added CR comments, small nits. overall looks good.

Samir K.: if 429s persist after adjustments, next step is to add short-lived KV cache for the prefix to reduce auth calls per user. I can prototype this today.

Maria T.: update 1765440600: after 25m the 429 rate dropped ~85% and tail latency improved. no regressions in other services. will merge PR after Alex's final review and schedule a gradual prod rollout tomorrow morning. thanks all. :thumbsup:
